title: Elysium Outpost
simulationNotice: Fictional expedition. Resource rates, route lengths, growth forecasts and shelter estimates are simulation values for planning. NASA sources explain the science; they do not validate this outpost or endorse the game.

prologue.title: Earth · Mission briefing
briefing: Cape Canaveral. Kaelen Reeves, 24, is the youngest astronaut chosen for this fictional commissioning team.
Robotic builders spent 14 months assembling Elysium Outpost. Its buildings stand ready. Now someone must prove that the systems can work together.
prologue.flightDirector: Robotic teams built it. Your job is to prove it works. Explore the region. Test the systems. Show us your plan. The next crew's expedition gets approved when that outpost is ready.
prologue.launchNote: Fictional Earth launch, space journey and arrival beside Elysium Outpost. Cuts compress the trip.
prologue.timeJump: Seven months later · Elysium Outpost, Mars
tutorial: WASD or the touch stick moves Kaelen. Space jumps.
Drag or swipe to look around. V changes the camera.
E interacts with a nearby station. F boards the deployed crew rover.
Caps Lock or Atlas opens the map. Follow the mission location marker.
Take your time. You can pause, explore or retry. No countdown can end your expedition.

solarDust.title: NASA/JPL · InSight’s solar-panel dust clearing
solarDust.claim: Dust reduces solar output. InSight used wind-carried sand to remove some dust in 2021; the game's handheld brush is a fictional maintenance activity.

eclss.title: NASA · Environmental Control and Life Support Systems
eclss.claim: Water recovery treats wastewater. Electrolysis separates water into hydrogen and oxygen. Air revitalization removes cabin carbon dioxide.

cdra.title: NASA · Carbon Dioxide technical brief
cdra.claim: ISS scrubber beds alternate capture and regeneration. One bed can clean air while another is heated and exposed to vacuum.

plants.title: NASA · Growing Plants in Space
plants.claim: Veggie supports plant experiments including lettuce. The Advanced Plant Habitat has grown dwarf wheat; light and water require careful control.

radishes.title: NASA · Astronauts Harvest Radish Crop
radishes.claim: The Advanced Plant Habitat radish experiment used a 27-day growth period. A seven-sol game forecast is not a real harvest schedule.

curiositySol.title: NASA · Sol 3056–3057: Perched on top…
curiositySol.claim: The March 10, 2021 update describes the Nontron drilling plan and observations near Mont Mercou in Gale Crater.

curiosityNavigation.title: NASA · Curiosity at Cooperstown
curiosityNavigation.claim: Curiosity can select paths between designated waypoints using its onboard navigation cameras. People on Earth plan its mission.

perseveranceLanding.title: NASA · Octavia E. Butler Landing
perseveranceLanding.claim: Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater on February 18, 2021. The game's marker represents that historical event, not a live location.

communications.title: NASA · Mars Relay Network
communications.claim: Earth–Mars distance changes with their orbits. One-way radio travel time is roughly 3 to 22 minutes, depending on their positions.

sep2017Mars.title: NASA/JPL · September 2017 Mars solar storm
sep2017Mars.claim: NASA reported a September 11, 2017 event with enhanced Mars auroras and unusually high surface radiation measured by Curiosity.

donki2017Earth.title: NASA CCMC DONKI · September 2017 archive notification
donki2017Earth.claim: The notification identifies 2017-09-10T16:45:00-SEP-001 as a GOES13 near-Earth >10 MeV particle event. It is not a Mars surface dose record.

shielding.title: NASA · Protecting astronauts from space radiation
shielding.claim: Shielding protection depends on the radiation, material and amount of matter. Adding appropriate shielding can reduce exposure; it is not complete protection.

marsTrek.title: NASA · Mars Trek
marsTrek.claim: Mars Trek supports exploration of real planetary surface data. Fictional mission routes and local sensors are game additions.

missions.title: Welcome to Elysium
briefing: Welcome to your Mars home! Explore the base and find the places that keep the crew safe.
At the command tablet, unpack the supplies. Then visit the airlock, garage and greenhouse.
missions.wakeText: A new home on Mars. Let’s see what the builders left us!
objectives: Enter the habitat airlock.
Read the command terminal and cargo manifest.
Visit the garage and a greenhouse.

scienceNotes.title: Science Note · Connected systems
scienceNotes.text: The habitat needs clean water, oxygen and carbon dioxide removal. These are separate jobs that share power and equipment.

logOptions: The buildings look finished. Testing them together is my job.
I checked the reserves before switching anything on.
Someone wrote 'Good luck up there' on the manifest. I kept the note.

missions.title: Wake the Grid
briefing: The solar panels need your help. Find the broken cable, match the wires and brush away the dust.
Back at the command tablet, share the power between the home, rover, plants and spare battery.
missions.wakeText: The panels are dusty and one cable is broken. Time to fix them.
objectives: Trace the solar wiring and repair Cluster C.
Brush the dusty panels so sunlight can reach the cells.
Choose a power allocation at the command terminal.
Review the overnight reserve forecast.

scienceNotes.title: Mission Notes · Power balance
scienceNotes.text: A battery stores energy for later. If charging, lighting and life support use more than the array supplies, the battery reserve falls. These capacity numbers are simulation values.

scienceNotes.title: Mission Notes · Dust and sunlight
scienceNotes.text: Dust on solar cells blocks sunlight and reduces the electricity they produce. InSight removed some dust using wind-carried sand. Our brushing exercise is fictional: real spacecraft need carefully engineered cleaning methods. Cleaning helps future production; it does not instantly recharge a battery.

logOptions: I traced the cable instead of guessing at the fault.
I left room in the battery for things I could not predict.
I chose what to power first, and recorded what would have to wait.

missions.title: Every Drop, Every Breath
briefing: Let’s make clean water and breathing air. Turn the pipes, fix the gauge and put the water filters in order.
Then separate oxygen bubbles and give the air cleaner a fresh filter. Watch how these jobs help each other.
missions.wakeText: The crew needs water and fresh air. Let’s get both flowing.
objectives: Compare the faulty humidity sensor with the reference and calibrate it.
Set water recovery and oxygen generation separately.
Schedule carbon dioxide scrubber regeneration.

scienceNotes.title: Science Note · Water recovery
scienceNotes.text: Used water and moisture from cabin air can be collected and treated. Recovery saves supplies; it does not create unlimited water.

scienceNotes.title: Science Note · Oxygen generation
scienceNotes.text: An electrolyser uses electricity to split water into oxygen and hydrogen. Making more oxygen needs more water and power.

scienceNotes.title: Science Note · Carbon dioxide removal
scienceNotes.text: Scrubber material captures carbon dioxide from the air. Real ISS beds take turns cleaning and regenerating. Reduced capacity here represents a fictional maintenance condition.

logOptions: I checked a second reading before trusting the sensor.
Making oxygen and removing carbon dioxide are different jobs.
I matched the water plan to the people, crops and oxygen unit.

missions.title: The First Harvest
briefing: Try growing a little food on Mars! Plant a seed and give it light and water.
Compare two trial pots. Help the thirsty plant before choosing how much of the base’s supplies to use.
missions.wakeText: What helps a plant grow? Let’s try it on the growing tablet.
objectives: Visit Greenhouse 1 and inspect the labelled trays.
Choose a crop-care plan and review the seven-sol forecast.
Compare growth, water use and power demand.

scienceNotes.title: Science Note · Growing food
scienceNotes.text: NASA has grown lettuce in Veggie and radishes and dwarf wheat in the Advanced Plant Habitat. Real crops take weeks. This forecast accelerates growth and cannot replace a complete food supply.

logOptions: That never gets old.
More light did not help when the roots needed water.
A small crop with a steady supply can be a useful start.

missions.title: Beyond the Base
briefing: A sensor outside the base has stopped sending messages. Trace a rover route and check you have power for the trip home.
Drive there, uncover the sensor and tune it. Collect rocks in labelled boxes, then look closely at them in the lab.
missions.wakeText: Pack the rover. There is a sensor to find and rocks to explore.
objectives: Choose a route and check the shared rover battery.
Drive to the field sensor and diagnose its fault.
Restore the sensor, collect a sample and analyse it at the lab.

scienceNotes.title: Mission Notes · Route scale
scienceNotes.text: The 2.1, 3.4 and 4.8 km route labels are fictional planning distances. The playable routes are shortened to about 280, 600 and 730 metres. They are not measured NASA traverses.

scienceNotes.title: Science Note · Curiosity heritage
scienceNotes.text: Curiosity explores Gale Crater. It can navigate between waypoints, while people on Earth plan its work. The Sol 3057 marker refers to a 2021 observation period near Mont Mercou. Its nearby game placement is fictional.

logOptions: I planned the return before driving away.
The inspection mattered more than my first guess.
A careful route kept energy available for the habitat.

missions.title: A Message from the Sun
briefing: Let’s practise getting ready for a solar storm. This is a pretend drill based on an old NASA event.
Fix the shelter fan and backup power. Build up the walls and try a gentle particle-wave experiment.
missions.wakeText: A practice warning from the Sun. Let’s prepare a safe place.
objectives: Review the historical event and identify what was measured at Earth and at Mars.
Check the shelter's ventilation and power supply.
Choose shielding and compare the simulation estimates.

scienceNotes.title: Science Note · Archived event
scienceNotes.text: NASA reported a strong solar event at Mars on September 11, 2017. Curiosity measured increased surface radiation. This drill reuses the historical context, not a live warning or measured dose forecast.

scienceNotes.title: Science Note · Two locations
scienceNotes.text: The linked DONKI particle record was observed near Earth by GOES13 on September 10, 2017. An Earth particle-flux reading is not the radiation dose an astronaut would receive on Mars.

scienceNotes.title: Science Note · Shelter
scienceNotes.text: Shielding can reduce additional exposure. It does not erase dose already received. Closing an airlock keeps air inside; protection from energetic particles also depends on the surrounding material.

logOptions: A shelter needs air and power as well as thick walls.
The archive helped me prepare without pretending a drill was an emergency.
I spent rover energy on shielding and allowed time to recharge.

missions.title: First Light
briefing: Your base is nearly ready! Pack the plan and a backup, then tune in to Mission Control.
Try one pretend night. If equipment stops working, open its repair game. You can pause and try again.
missions.wakeText: One last check before the next crew arrives. We can do this.
objectives: Submit a complete operating plan and acknowledge the review.
Choose a contingency for reduced solar power.
Diagnose the overnight fault and keep essential systems supplied.

scienceNotes.title: Science Note · Distant decisions
scienceNotes.text: Earth and Mars keep moving. Their separation and radio delay change. Signals can take roughly 3 to 22 minutes each way. Kaelen must make local decisions; the game does not make you wait.

scienceNotes.title: Mission Notes · Safe test
scienceNotes.text: The night test advances when you choose the next step. Reserve bars show supplies, not a countdown. A weak plan enters safe mode with an explanation and a retry.

logOptions: I explained my decisions instead of only following the checklist.
My backup plan mattered when one system changed.
A retry showed me what to improve. It did not erase what I had learned.

grid.label: Charge the rover first
grid.decision: Put extra power into rover charging while lighting one greenhouse.
grid.outcome: The rover can be ready sooner and seedlings get light, but overnight reserve is thinner.
grid.why: Fast charging and crop lights draw from the same supply as essential systems.

grid.label: Share with everyone
grid.decision: Share power across the rover, one greenhouse and a quiet lab.
grid.outcome: Charging takes longer while more energy remains available for the night.
grid.why: Lower simultaneous demand leaves a larger margin for unexpected needs.

grid.label: Help the plants first
grid.decision: Send the available power to both greenhouses before rover charging.
grid.outcome: Both crop areas can start, but the rover stays low until you change the plan or advance a charging cycle.
grid.why: The same solar energy cannot run every high-demand task at once.

grid.label: Save spare power
grid.decision: Prioritise essential habitat systems and store the rest.
grid.outcome: The habitat has a wide safety margin. Crop progress and rover readiness must wait.
grid.why: Delaying optional loads is a valid plan. You can revise it when you need to travel.

water.label: Save more power
water.decision: Use the lowest-power water recovery setting.
water.outcome: Recovery uses little power, but stored water must cover more of the demand.
water.why: Lower recovery saves energy now while reducing the amount returned to storage.

water.label: Steady water flow
water.decision: Balance water recovery with normal habitat demand.
water.outcome: The supply can support the daily plan more steadily.
water.why: Matching recovery to use avoids paying for output the habitat does not need.

water.label: Recover more water
water.decision: Recover more water using a higher power setting.
water.outcome: More water returns to use, with a larger electricity cost. Giving it all to crops still leaves less for the habitat.
water.why: Recovered water is shared by people, the oxygen unit and plants.

oxygen.label: Save water and power
oxygen.decision: Use a low electrolyser rate while relying on the oxygen reserve.
oxygen.outcome: Power and water use stay low. The oxygen reserve needs closer review.
oxygen.why: A lower production rate may not replace everything the habitat uses.

oxygen.label: Steady air supply
oxygen.decision: Match oxygen production to the normal habitat plan.
oxygen.outcome: Oxygen supply and resource use stay balanced in the simulation.
oxygen.why: The electrolyser needs both clean water and electricity.

oxygen.label: Make more oxygen
oxygen.decision: Build oxygen reserve with a higher electrolyser rate.
oxygen.outcome: Oxygen reserve improves, but power and water available to other systems fall.
oxygen.why: Extra oxygen is useful only if the shared water and energy budget can support it.

scrubber.label: Keep a spare filter ready
scrubber.decision: Plan a regeneration period while the other bed handles the air.
scrubber.outcome: Carbon dioxide removal continues with a planned margin.
scrubber.why: Alternating beds is how real regenerative systems avoid stopping all air cleaning at once.

scrubber.label: Clean the filter now
scrubber.outcome: The bed is refreshed sooner. Watch the reduced-capacity warning in this fictional maintenance case.
scrubber.why: Timing a shared-system task matters as much as choosing the task.

greenhouse.label: One steady crop
greenhouse.decision: Give one greenhouse steady light and water.
greenhouse.outcome: A modest crop can develop with a manageable demand on the habitat.
greenhouse.why: Plants need a balance of inputs, not the maximum of one input.

greenhouse.label: More crops, more supplies
greenhouse.decision: Raise the light and irrigation targets in one greenhouse.
greenhouse.outcome: The forecast can improve if water recovery supports it. Other systems have less spare capacity.
greenhouse.why: High light without enough water slows growth instead of guaranteeing more food.

greenhouse.label: Share the growing space
greenhouse.decision: Spread the available light and water between two crop areas.
greenhouse.outcome: More trays can grow, but each receives less. Unrepaired water losses may limit both.
greenhouse.why: Twice as many plants also need a reliable shared supply.

greenhouse.label: Use packed food for now
greenhouse.decision: Keep cultivation small and preserve supplies for the habitat.
greenhouse.outcome: Stored rations remain the main food source. This is a valid low-demand plan.
greenhouse.why: A commissioning mission can prove safe operation without making the base fully food-independent.

route.label: Short, rough trail
route.outcome: The predicted energy cost is lowest if the rover avoids damage. Steep ground and rocks need care.
route.why: A shorter path can save energy while increasing the chance of repairs.

route.label: Dusty ridge trail
route.outcome: The planning estimate uses moderate energy. Dust exposure can reduce the assumed solar contribution.
route.why: Sunlight and terrain both affect an expedition plan. The dust penalty is simulated.

route.label: Long, gentle trail
route.decision: Follow the longer, flatter basin route.
route.outcome: The route has the lowest planned damage risk but needs the largest energy allowance and a full charging cycle.
route.why: Gentler ground can reduce risk while extra distance uses more stored energy.

sensor.label: Clear the buried sensor head
sensor.decision: Use the inspection evidence to remove the sand covering the sensor.
sensor.outcome: The clear sensor can resume measurements after its connection is checked.
sensor.why: A covered sensor may be working electrically but unable to observe its surroundings.

sensor.label: Replace electronics first
sensor.decision: Treat the silence as an electronics fault before clearing the sensor.
sensor.outcome: The buried head still blocks useful readings. Inspect it again and try the other explanation.
sensor.why: Replacing a part does not fix a different cause. A second attempt costs no progress.

shielding.label: More wall layers
shielding.decision: Check services and haul extra shielding with the rover.
shielding.outcome: The drill predicts the lowest additional exposure, using rover charge that must later be restored.
shielding.why: Extra appropriate material can improve protection, but it takes transport resources.

shielding.label: One extra wall layer
shielding.decision: Add some shielding while relying on the existing habitat structure.
shielding.outcome: The drill predicts intermediate protection with less hauling.
shielding.why: Protection and transport effort can be balanced. Review the estimate for the chosen scenario.

shielding.label: Use the existing walls
shielding.decision: Use the current shelter without hauling more material.
shielding.outcome: This costs no rover energy and gives the least protection of these plans. Review it against the drill's event level.
shielding.why: A low-cost choice can be reasonable for a mild scenario, but it is not complete radiation protection.

contingency.label: Keep a spare battery
contingency.decision: Keep stored energy available before starting optional work.
contingency.outcome: The overnight test starts with a larger margin for essential systems.
contingency.why: A reserve makes it easier to absorb an unexpected demand.

contingency.label: Dim the plant lights
contingency.decision: Reduce crop lighting if solar supply is lower than planned.
contingency.outcome: Crops may grow more slowly while habitat essentials retain power.
contingency.why: A flexible load can be reduced before a critical life-support load.

contingency.label: Slow the rover charger
contingency.decision: Let rover charging wait when reliable supply falls.
contingency.outcome: The rover becomes ready later while more power remains for the habitat.
contingency.why: A charging schedule can move without changing the energy required by essential systems.

clear-panels.label: Clear the wind-blown panel dust
clear-panels.outcome: The panel surface is clear. The next sol no longer loses power yield to this dust.
clear-panels.why: Dust blocks some sunlight. Cleaning restores available production; it does not instantly fill a battery.

cargo-read.label: Unpack the supply locker
cargo-read.outcome: Supplies are sorted and ready to find. You kept the builders’ good-luck note.
cargo-read.why: Putting supplies in the right place helps the crew find them when they need them.

solar-trace.label: Find the broken cable
solar-trace.outcome: The fault is narrowed to a loose connector.
solar-trace.why: Following the power path avoids replacing working equipment.

solar-connect.label: Repair Cluster C wiring
solar-connect.outcome: The repaired cluster can contribute to reliable solar supply.
solar-connect.why: A complete electrical connection lets generated power reach the shared grid.

solar-clean.label: Brush the dusty solar panels
solar-clean.outcome: The cleaned panel surface is ready to collect sunlight for the shared grid.
solar-clean.why: Removing dust lets more sunlight reach the cells. Cleaning prepares future production; it does not instantly refill a battery.

water-compare.label: Get water flowing
water-compare.outcome: Water flows through the loop. The two gauges do not agree—one needs checking.
water-compare.why: A checked reference helps us spot a faulty sensor before trusting it.

water-calibrate.label: Fix the water gauge
water-calibrate.outcome: The gauge now matches the checked reading. Less water is wasted.
water-calibrate.why: A bad reading can make good equipment do the wrong job.

forecast-review.label: Help the thirsty plants
forecast-review.outcome: You helped the trial plants by balancing light and water.
forecast-review.why: Extra light cannot help a plant whose roots are too dry. Real crops grow over weeks.

sensor-restore.label: Wake the field sensor
sensor-restore.outcome: The cleared sensor resumes useful readings after its connection is checked.
sensor-restore.why: A working observation improves the game's planning confidence; it is not a guarantee of real weather.

sample-collect.label: Collect rock samples
sample-collect.outcome: The rocks are sealed in labelled boxes for the journey home.
sample-collect.why: Labels keep track of where samples came from, and clean boxes keep them apart.

sample-analyse.label: Look closely at your rocks
sample-analyse.outcome: You grouped the rocks by what you could see: smooth, grainy or full of holes.
sample-analyse.why: Looking closely is the first step. A texture alone cannot prove which minerals or signs of life a rock contains.

archive-review.label: Practise a Sun alert
archive-review.outcome: The practice warning is understood. Next, prepare the shelter.
archive-review.why: Warnings give crews a chance to move to a more protected place. This is an old event used for practice.

ventilation-check.label: Fix the shelter fan
ventilation-check.outcome: The fan moves cabin air through the filter and back around the room.
ventilation-check.why: Mars air is not safe to breathe. The shelter keeps its own air inside.

shelter-power.label: Connect backup power
shelter-power.outcome: The shelter's essential electrical supply has been checked.
shelter-power.why: Protection is useful only when the space can support its occupants.

plan-submit.label: Pack the base plan
plan-submit.outcome: Your base plan is ready for Mission Control.
plan-submit.why: Checking the systems together helps us notice what each one needs.

review-ack.label: Catch Mission Control’s message
review-ack.outcome: Mission Control’s message is received. You can try the night test.
review-ack.why: Radio signals take time to cross space. The story skips the long wait.

faults.title: Heater surge
chain: Crop lighting loses its margin and plants receive a cold warning.

choices.label: Reduce the heater load
choices.outcome: Power is freed while the simulated habitat cools gradually.
choices.why: Saving power here means accepting less thermal margin. Check essential temperatures before the next step.

choices.label: Reduce greenhouse lighting
choices.outcome: The habitat stays warm while the crops receive less light and may be stressed.
choices.why: Reducing a flexible crop load can protect immediate habitat needs.

choices.label: Regenerate with backup air cleaning
choices.outcome: The bed is restored while the backup handles the air.
choices.why: Fixing the cause reduces the need to keep raising ventilation power.

choices.label: Reduce ventilation without fixing the bed
choices.outcome: Power demand falls, but the air-quality problem remains. Safe mode explains the issue and allows a retry.
choices.why: Saving power is not enough if carbon dioxide removal still cannot meet demand.

faults.title: Water pump stall
chain: The oxygen unit loses part of its water supply.
The reserve indicator shows the shared supply getting smaller.

choices.label: Restart the pump at the lab
choices.outcome: Water can flow again after the physical restart.
choices.why: Oxygen generation depends on a working clean-water supply.

choices.label: Protect habitat water after the restart
choices.outcome: Less water goes to crops while habitat and oxygen reserves recover.
choices.why: Temporarily reducing an optional demand helps the shared supply rebuild.

conservative.title: Ready · Conservative plan
conservative.flightDirector: Elysium is ready. You prioritised margins. That is smart engineering far from the nearest repair shop.
conservative.why: You kept larger reserves and accepted fewer active systems. Your logs explain what can wait.

balanced.title: Ready · Balanced plan
balanced.flightDirector: Elysium is ready. You built a sustainable plan and explained how its systems support one another.
balanced.why: You matched useful work to dependable supply, with a plan for changes.

productive.title: Ready · Productive plan
productive.flightDirector: Elysium is ready. You expanded what the outpost can do. You understood the extra work and the tighter reserves.
productive.why: You supported more active systems and prepared for their larger shared demands.

finalLogOptions: I know how these systems depend on each other now.
The next crew will find a plan they can understand and improve.
Commissioning is complete. There is still a horizon to explore.

initial: Solar array 73% · Panel Cluster C fault
statusText.warning: Combined demand exceeds reliable supply. Individual tests passed; integrated operation is not verified.
statusText.cargoManifest: Construction cargo · Habitat panels, seed trays, cables, filters and repair tools. Margin note: Good luck up there.
reviewQuestions: What keeps essential systems supplied when solar power stops?
Which optional load will you reduce first?
What evidence supports your water, rover and shelter plan?
statusText.reviewNotice: Mission Control transmission · reply delay skipped. These are human review questions, not a live conversation.
statusText.safeMode: Test paused in safe mode. Your expedition and logs are saved. Review what happened, adjust the plan and retry. The point is knowing what to do when things are not perfect.
statusText.reserveNotice: Resource reserve, not a countdown. The test advances only when you choose.
statusText.endingTransmission: We have reviewed your operating plan, test results and logs. You have shown how this outpost can support its next crew.
statusText.completion: Commissioning complete. The door is still open if you want to keep exploring.
statusText.forecastNotice: Accelerated seven-sol simulation. This is a planning forecast, not a real crop growth schedule.
statusText.routeNotice: Fictional route estimates. Planning kilometres are shortened for play; the world map uses its own stated regional scale.
statusText.archiveDate: Mars event: September 11, 2017. Near-Earth DONKI particle observation: September 10, 2017.
statusText.archiveNotice: Archived observations, not a current alert. Radiation comparison values are invented estimates over the same drill interval; they are not measured astronaut doses.
statusText.shieldingNotice: A shelter reduces additional exposure. It does not subtract dose already received. Material and thickness matter; a closed airlock alone is not a radiation shield.
statusText.fictionNotice: Kaelen Reeves and Elysium Outpost are fictional. The commissioning history and seven-month journey belong to this story.

water.title: Water recovery loop
water.note: Treatment and a quality check are required before reuse. The faulty humidity sensor is a fictional troubleshooting exercise.

oxygen.title: Water electrolysis
oxygen.note: Oxygen generation uses water and power. It does not remove cabin carbon dioxide.

co2.title: Carbon dioxide removal
co2.note: Regeneration releases captured carbon dioxide so a bed can work again. This is a separate process from making oxygen.

crops.title: Balanced crop care
crops.note: The seven-sol forecast is accelerated and simplified. Turning light to maximum does not guarantee growth.

shielding.title: Shelter comparison
shielding.note: These are simulation estimates, not NASA measurements. Protection reduces new exposure; accumulated dose stays recorded.
